methodological_rigor.justification: The study uses complementary single-cell transcriptomics, multiplex immunofluorescence, spatial transcriptomics, T cell clonality analysis, in vitro coculture, ELISA, and independent bulk transcriptomic survival cohorts to study lymph node organization in reactive nodes, FL, and DLBCL. Methods are detailed for tissue processing, cell sorting, batch correction, differential expression, transcription-factor inference, ligand-receptor modeling, spatial point-pattern analysis, deconvolution, survival modeling, and coculture assays. The main limitation is exploratory observational design with no sample-size predetermination, limited spatial transcriptomics cores, no randomization for primary tissue processing, and no sex- or gender-based analysis. Statistical methods are generally appropriate, with multiple-comparison correction used in several omics analyses and validation across independent DLBCL cohorts, but causal inference from human tissue remains limited.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: The manuscript is primarily an observational translational study using patient tissue and independent bulk cohorts, with survival analyses in DLBCL datasets, so Oxford level 2b is the closest fit for the clinical association component. The clinical relevance is moderate because loss of homeostatic chemokines and inferred FDC fractions are associated with adverse survival and may illuminate lymphoma progression. However, the study does not test a therapeutic intervention, diagnostic assay, or prospective prognostic model in patients, so immediate clinical applicability is limited.

reporting_quality.justification: STROBE is appropriate for the observational patient-sample and cohort analyses. The manuscript reports consent, ethics approval, sample handling, inclusion of all available samples, no sample-size predetermination due to exploratory design, preprocessing thresholds, statistical tests, correction methods, external bulk cohorts, and survival modeling. Limitations include small spatial transcriptomics sample numbers and incomplete demographic design considerations. A Zenodo data record is cited and figure source data are provided, supporting stronger reproducibility than most exploratory tissue studies, although full executable code availability is not clearly described.

novelty_literature.justification: Prior work has described lymph node stromal cells, lymphoma stromal remodeling, and single-cell lymphoma microenvironments, and the manuscript cites several direct comparators. The novelty is the integrated model linking stromal chemokine reprogramming, tumor-reactive T cell inflammatory feedback, spatial disorganization, and survival associations across reactive nodes, FL, and DLBCL. The conceptual advance is meaningful, but it builds on an active literature in stromal immunology and lymphoma spatial profiling rather than establishing a wholly new disease mechanism from scratch.

writing_presentation.justification: The abstract clearly frames lymph node architecture, disease entities, methods, mechanism, and survival relevance. The Methods section is detailed enough to evaluate complex single-cell, spatial, and bulk-transcriptomic analyses, and figure captions report cohorts, sample sizes, tests, and key definitions. The Results narrative is coherent, moving from spatial organization to stromal chemokines, inflammatory reprogramming, in silico attraction potential, and survival associations. Some terminology and computational methods are dense, but this reflects the technical scope more than poor presentation.

key_strengths: Integrates single-cell, spatial, multiplex imaging, clonality, coculture, plasma chemokine, and independent bulk-survival datasets.
Provides a coherent mechanistic model linking stromal chemokine loss, inflammatory T cell feedback, tissue disorganization, and lymphoma progression.
Independent DLBCL bulk cohorts support the survival relevance of homeostatic chemokine expression and FDC abundance.
Strong computational reporting with named tools, thresholds, correction methods, and source data availability.
key_concerns: The study is exploratory and observational, with no prospective validation cohort or intervention testing the proposed mechanism.
Spatial transcriptomics appears limited to one FL and one DLBCL tissue core, constraining generalizability of spatial findings.
No sample-size predetermination was performed and some assays use small patient numbers.
Clinical utility of the chemokine or FDC survival associations is not established as an independent deployable prognostic model.
chief_reviewer.rationale: The manuscript is a strong translational biology study with a well-supported spatial and immunologic mechanism. Tier 1 with minor revisions is plausible, with residual concerns focused on exploratory design and limited prospective clinical validation.
